newsitem.title: USA: Nebraska wheat condition seen aided by moisture.
newsitem.headline: Nebraska wheat condition seen aided by moisture.

text.p: Heavy snow across much of Nebraska largely halted fieldwork in the week to Sunday while the moisture aided the winter wheat crop, according to the state's Agricultural Statistics Service.
"The effects of recent wind and low temperatures were not fully known. However, moisture received should improve crop prospects," the report said.
Nebraska's wheat was rated six percent excellent, 49 percent good, 40 percent fair and five percent poor, barely changed from a week earlier.
The additional moisture, although beneficial for wheat, raised concerns about flooding along the Missouri River.
"Corn producers were waiting for soils to dry and warm up before planting this year's crop," the report said.
The snowstorm caused further stress to livestock.
"Some calves were beginning to show signs of scours due to the cold, wet conditions. Cattle and sheep losses were reported in the Panhandle," the report said.
Pasture and range condition was rated seven percent excellent, 58 percent good, 32 percent poor and three percent poor.
